name: Structured Family Caregiving (SFC)
summary: Structured Family Caregiving is a service on Indiana's PathWays for Aging, Health and Wellness, and Traumatic Brain Injury waivers. A family caregiver who lives with the member works with an approved SFC agency, which provides a caregiver coach and nurse oversight and pays the caregiver a daily stipend. It is the main Indiana option that lets a spouse or a parent of a minor child be paid.
who_qualifies: Enrolled in Indiana Medicaid and in the PathWays for Aging (age 60+), Health and Wellness (disability, under 60) or Traumatic Brain Injury waiver.
Needs a nursing-facility level of care, set by an Area Agency on Aging assessment.
Lives full time with the chosen caregiver in a private home.
The SFC level (1, 2 or 3) is based on how much daily help the member needs.

who_can_be_paid.adult_children_relatives: yes — adult children, other relatives, guardians, POAs and health care representatives may provide SFC.
who_can_be_paid.spouse: yes — FSSA lists the spouse of the waiver recipient as allowed to provide structured family care.
who_can_be_paid.parent_of_minor: yes — on the Health and Wellness waiver, biological or adoptive parents, guardians, foster parents and stepparents of a minor may provide SFC.
who_can_be_paid.live_together: required — the caregiver and member must live together.

pay.detail: Effective July 1, 2025 the state pays the SFC agency $77.54/day (Level 1), $99.71 (Level 2) or $133.44 (Level 3). Agencies must spend at least 60% of the daily rate on the caregiver stipend and direct-care costs, which per FSSA also covers caregiver coaching, nurse supervision and respite. That puts the caregiver's tax-free stipend at roughly $46–$80/day or less, depending on the agency.

hours_or_budget: SFC is paid per day, not per hour. The level is set from the member's assessed needs in the service plan.

waitlist.detail: PathWays and Health and Wellness hit federally approved capacity in April 2024 and use waiting lists; FSSA posts counts on its waiver waiting list page (6,836 on the Health and Wellness list as of August 2026).

self_directed_or_agency: Agency. The caregiver must be enrolled with an approved SFC provider agency that supervises the home and pays the stipend.
how_to_apply: Contact your local Area Agency on Aging (INconnect Alliance, 800-986-3505) for intake and a level-of-care screening.
Apply for Indiana Medicaid through FSSA and get placed on the waiver waiting list if slots are full.
When invited, accept within 30 days and finish the service plan within 180 days.
Ask your care manager or care coordinator for SFC and choose an SFC agency.

faqs.q: Can I get paid to care for my spouse in Indiana?
faqs.a: Yes, through Structured Family Caregiving if you live together and your spouse is on a qualifying waiver. Spouses cannot be paid for attendant care.

faqs.q: Can a parent get paid to care for a disabled child in Indiana?
faqs.a: Yes, through SFC on the Health and Wellness waiver. Parents of minors cannot provide attendant care since July 1, 2024.

faqs.q: How much does structured family caregiving pay in Indiana?
faqs.a: The agency gets $77.54 to $133.44 a day by level. At least 60% must go to the caregiver and direct-care costs, so the stipend is often about $46 to $80 a day.
SFC stipends are commonly treated as tax-free difficulty-of-care payments under IRS Notice 2014-7 when the caregiver lives with the member. Ask your agency or a tax adviser.

faqs.q: Why is there a waiting list?
faqs.a: PathWays and Health and Wellness reached their federal slot limits in 2024. FSSA invites people off the list as slots open.

name: Attendant Care (PathWays and Health & Wellness Waivers)
summary: Attendant Care is an hourly in-home help service on Indiana's PathWays for Aging, Health and Wellness, and Traumatic Brain Injury waivers. It can be delivered through an agency or self-directed. Adult children and many other relatives can be paid attendants, but since July 1, 2024 spouses and parents of minor children cannot.
who_qualifies: Enrolled in Indiana Medicaid and the PathWays for Aging, Health and Wellness or Traumatic Brain Injury waiver.
Needs a nursing-facility level of care.
Needs hands-on help with daily tasks, approved in the service plan.

who_can_be_paid.adult_children_relatives: yes — parents of an adult, stepparents, other relatives, POAs and health care representatives may provide attendant care; a legal guardian of an adult is capped at 40 hours a week.
who_can_be_paid.spouse: no — since July 1, 2024 a spouse may not provide attendant care (spouses can use SFC instead).
who_can_be_paid.parent_of_minor: no — biological or adoptive parents and guardians of a minor may not provide attendant care; a stepparent may.
who_can_be_paid.live_together: optional — the attendant may live with the member or elsewhere.

pay.detail: Effective July 1, 2025 the state pays agencies $34.36 an hour for attendant care, and agencies must spend at least 70% of it on the direct worker's wages and related costs. The worker's actual hourly wage is set by the agency.

hours_or_budget: Hours are approved in the waiver service plan based on assessed need.

waitlist.detail: PathWays and Health and Wellness use waiting lists since reaching capacity in April 2024.

self_directed_or_agency: Either. Attendant care can be agency-based or participant-directed, but legally responsible individuals (spouses, parents of minors) are barred from self-directed attendant care by Indiana Code 12-10-17.1-10(b).
how_to_apply: Contact your local Area Agency on Aging (800-986-3505) for intake and screening.
Apply for Indiana Medicaid and join the waiver waiting list if needed.
When enrolled, ask your care manager to add attendant care and choose an agency or self-direction.

faqs.q: Can an adult child be paid for attendant care in Indiana?
faqs.a: Yes. Adult children and other relatives can be paid attendants.

faqs.q: Why can't my spouse be my attendant anymore?
faqs.a: Indiana changed its waivers on July 1, 2024 so spouses and parents of minors cannot provide attendant care. They can provide Structured Family Caregiving instead.
The agency gets $34.36 an hour and must use at least 70% on the worker. Your wage depends on the agency.
A legal guardian of an adult can provide up to 40 hours of attendant care a week. Other attendants can cover more hours.
